national_raw_news.title: 7 hours ago | National 404 PM Modi inaugurates IMC 2026; says 5G connectivity reaches every district
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi. The four-day event, which began yesterday, showcases India’s remarkable progress in telecommunications, digital connectivity and technological innovation. The theme of IMC 2026 is ‘Scale Without Boundaries’, reflecting India’s growing capabilities in digital innovation, next-generation connectivity and technology-led growth. Inaugurating the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress, PM Modi said the platform has witnessed the evolution of India’s telecom sector and digital connectivity over the years. He said the platform has emerged as a showcase of India’s progress and aspirations. The Prime Minister said 5G connectivity has reached every district of the country. He added that there are now more than five lakh 50 thousand base stations operating 5G connectivity across India. He said the government is now working to connect around 25 crore students through various digital and online education platforms. Prime Minister Modi said digital connectivity has powered education, healthcare and government services. He said that even children in remote villages and those from poor families are now able to access quality knowledge. PM Modi said that over the past 10 to 12 years, mobile phones have emerged not only as a medium of modern communication but also as a crucial tool for good governance. PM Modi highlighted the growing importance of digital education in India through the DIKSHA platform. He said that during the COVID-19 period, DIKSHA recorded over 500 crore learning sessions and approximately six thousand crore learning minutes by July 2022. On the occasion, Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said that in 2014, one gigabyte of data cost 268 rupees, whereas today it costs only around eight rupees, making India one of the countries with the cheapest data in the world.

national_raw_news.title: 7 hours ago | National 480 FM Nirmala Sitharaman chairs 57th GST Council meeting in New Delhi
national_raw_news.content: The 57th GST Council meeting is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman is chairing the meeting. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Karnataka Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, and Finance Ministers of States and Union Territories are also attending the meeting. The GST Council meeting will discuss policy reforms to resolve GST disputes and improve the flow of input tax credit, with the aim of reducing the time and cost of compliance. Sources in the Finance Ministry said that the government will propose a five-pronged plan for the next set of reforms to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) system. These reforms are aimed at automating and easing many of the current administrative bottlenecks in the GST system and reducing the compliance burden, especially for small businesses. The five-pronged proposal covers process reforms, structural reforms, ease of living and doing business, exports of services, and e-commerce. Some of the key changes proposed involve automatic invoice matching between buyers and sellers, reducing paperwork around claiming input tax credits (ITC), reducing the number of times small taxpayers have to file returns, and removing multi-state registrations for small businesses. The last, 56th meeting of the GST Council was held in September last year. During the meeting, the Council approved rate rationalisation with a focus on the common man, labour-intensive industries, farmers and agriculture, health, and key drivers of the economy.
